thread:
Maya Chen: Quick design sync: new trace viewer export & drilldown mock ready — looking for UX + a11y nits. https://www.figma.com/file/trace-v4
Jordan Patel: First take: make export options explicit: "Export raw trace (JSON)", "Export table (CSV)", "Export bundle (.zip)". include size estimate before exporting.
Eli Navarro: Agree. Also add a toggle: "Include stack frames" for JSON export. customers sometimes only need spans.
Samir Khan: Accessibility: timeline color contrast is low. either increase contrast or add pattern overlays and ensure hover-only info is available via keyboard focus.
Maya Chen: Noted. Keyboard: we plan to support Tab to span, Enter to open detail panel, and "e" to open export modal. good?
Jordan Patel: Yes, and show a small "?" shortcut help overlay. For deep links, prefer copyable short link next to trace id with "Link copied" feedback.
Eli Navarro: Drilldown panel should show top metadata (method, path, status, duration) in a compact header so you don't need to open full span.
Samir Khan: For exports over 5MB or 1k spans show warning: "Large export — consider exporting visible spans". backend will return pre-signed URL; surface a notification when ready (aria-live).
ops-bot: Alert: spikes on billing-service at 02:11 UTC. sample correlation id: a1b2c3d4.
Maya Chen: ops-bot pin idea: drag an alert into viewer to auto-open traces near timestamp. quick for oncall. will prototype.
Jordan Patel: Small copy nit: use "correlation ID" capitalization everywhere. Also include correlation_id in exported metadata along with trace_short_url and signed_until.
Maya Chen: Great feedback — i'll iterate the Figma and post updates. checklist: export labels + size estimate, stack-frame toggle, higher-contrast/patterns, keyboard focus + shortcuts, copyable deep link, ops-bot drag-to-filter, aria-live notifications.
